newsitem.title: UK: UK gov't to change Prime Minister's question time.
newsitem.headline: UK gov't to change Prime Minister's question time.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said on Friday it will overhaul the format of Prime Minister's question time in the House of Commons.

The twice weekly sessions of 15 minutes, held on Tuesdays and Thursdays every week that Parliament has sat since 1961, will be replaced by a 30-minute session every Wednesday, a statement issued by the Cabinet Office said.
"The government is committed to reforming and modernising the House of Commons to make a parliament for the 21st century," Taylor said in a statement.
She said the government proposed to set up a new special Select Committee to review parliamentary procedures and consider further changes to question time.

Officials said a likely further change would be to replace "open" questions to the prime minister -- usually asking about his engagements for the day -- with questions on specific subjects. This would reduce the scope for MPs to ambush the prime minister by raising unexpected issues.

But Blair, despite addressing his cabinet ministers on first-name terms, does not intend to propose changing parliament's time-honoured tradition whereby MPs refer to each other as "honorable members" instead of by name.
The first prime minister's questions under the new format will be on May 21.

Because of Blair's determination to miss as few question sessions as possible, he will not be able to attend a ceremony in The Hague on May 28 commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan to rebuild war-torn western Europe, officials said.
